The documents describe installing and running Strata, a local model server for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, on a single NVIDIA or AMD GPU plus system RAM, serving OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible APIs at http://127.0.0.1:8080. Setup checks the PC: NVIDIA RTX 20/30/40/50 or AMD RX 7900/7800/7700/9060/9070/AI PRO R9700 with ≥12 GB VRAM, NVIDIA driver 580+, 32 GB+ RAM, ~80 GB disk, AVX2 CPU. The model download is 70–120 GB; setup is resumable. Flags include `--yes`, `--family` (qwen/swift/coder/unsloth), `--model` (IQ sizes, UD-IQ4_XS, UD-Q4_K_XL), `--context`, `--vision`, `--gpus`, `--backend cuda/hip`, `--data-dir`, `--host` plus `--api-key`, `--no-start`, `--setup`, `--check`. The server starts via `run-<model>.bat` or `.sh`, serves `/health`, `/v1/models`, `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/messages`, `/v1/responses`, and opens a browser UI. It enforces one-request-at-a-time decoding unless `--parallel` is set.

The AMD backends specifics: HIP supports gfx1100 (RX 7900 XT/XTX), gfx1101 (7800 XT/7700 XT), gfx1200 (9060 XT), gfx1201 (9070/9070 XT, AI PRO R9700), gfx1030 (6800/6900). Linux setup installs ROCm into `.venv` (~10 GB) or uses system ROCm 7, and compiles the engine 10–20 minutes. Windows uses prebuilt engine with ROCm 10.2 libraries, driver only, no compile; images are Linux-only. HipBLASLt tuning tables are architecture/version-specific; RDNA4 measured ~45 tok/s decode on R9700, ~31 on 9070 XT. gfx906 (MI50/MI60/Radeon VII) is an opt-in wave64 build with a CUDA-compat layer and measured ~58 tok/s on dual MI50s. The docs stress not exposing the server without an API key, keeping secrets, and using `--no-start` for automation.
